analysis:
Integration of the PR: dense Qwen3.5/3.8 requests gain an end-of-prompt (demandedLatest) checkpoint boundary in the SSD complete-checkpoint store. Changed code is small. EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift (head ~61-78) adds demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens. It returns the store's existing minEffectiveTokens only for the .paged backend, a dense Qwen35 model, and an SSDHybridCheckpointStore with a paged or native-quantized paged layout. Otherwise it returns nil. EngineV2Factory+Production.swift (head ~310) wires it into CBv2SchedulerConfig. The rest is docs, a changelog, tests that pin the gating (MoE, contiguous and nil-store return nil), and a libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (aee6ebb to 76ff231).

Threat relevance is T-041 (TB-007, A-001, SEC-035). The change only alters where prefill ranges end, so the checkpoint is persisted through the existing store. I saw no change to the HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt folding, DBK3 metadata/AAD, the 30-minute TTL, disk budget, KEK-wipe purge or the per-donation gate. The floor is not lowered. The effect is one more checkpoint per eligible request, bounded by the existing retention limits (first/target/latest), the write budget and the byte-admission guards. It is slightly finer same-account prefix-hit granularity, which stays within the accepted SEC-035 oracle. This is not a new disclosure class, so I raise no finding.

Unverified and carried forward (hence needs_deeper_review): the submodule bump contents are not supplied as a diff. That includes DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift and the scheduler and first-token projection logic, so the doc claims of token-exact restore and of unchanged store gating ('a request the store would write') cannot be confirmed. isDenseQwen35 is defined outside the evidence. Also unconfirmed is that the extra checkpoint cannot bypass the SSDPrefixCache.donate adoption and benefit gate or put prompt-derived plaintext into the metadata. Replay covered 49 of 83 units, so omitted units remain a coverage limit. No threat-model update appears necessary beyond optionally noting the extra end-of-prompt checkpoint under T-041.
